Ruhul Amin-II with Golam Mohiuddin, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner.

Abdul Quader Chowdhury ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Sayedul Hoque & others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment: 9. The lower Appellate Court on the basis of the report submitted on 9.2.1980 by the Commissioner appointed in Title Suit No. 63 of 1976 found that the land of DS Plot Nos. 22, 23, 24 of Khatian No. 162, DS Plot Nos. 93, 94, 95, 94/1 of Khatian No. 539, Plots Nos. 50, 51, 70 of Khatian No. 537, Plots Nos. 71, 72, 91, 96 of Khatian No. 538 and DS Plots Nos. 49, 52 and 69 of Khatian No. 536 of No. 258 Mouza Char Jubilee which was claimed by the father of the defendant No. 3 does not correspond to the land of the Diara Block Plot No. 81/123 and accordingly held that the order passed on 23.10.1968, Ext. A(a), in objection case No. 471 of 1968 was without any basis as the land of Idris Miah was not identical with the suit land. The learned District Judge also observed on the basis of Ext. A that while claiming the title and possession of the disputed land Idris Miah did not furnish the quantity of the land covered by his alleged pattan nor he disclosed the date when he took the settlement of the land appertaining to DS Khatian Nos. 162, 536, 537, 538 and 539 as his raiyati land which he alleged was incorporated in Block Plot No. 81/123 or Mouza Char Vvrapda. He also found that from the certified copy of the order dated 23.10.68, Ext. A(1) passed by the Objection Officer there was nothing to show that Idris Miah ever produced any paper in support of his claim of pattan from the Ex-land lords but Khatian No. 100 was opened in the name of Idris Miah for 32.50 acres of land showing 6 annas 13 gonads share in Plot No, 8'623. On consideration of Ext. 7, the lower appellate Court also found that. Diara Khatian No. 100 opened in the name of Idris Miah was illegal, collusive and without any basis and the Government claimed the entire 78.23 acres recorded in diara block Plot No. 81/123 as the Government khas land out of which the Government settled the land in dispute in perpetual lease to the different persons including the plaintiffs obtaining kabuliats from them and the claim of Abdul Kader Chowdhury, defendant No. 3 is not identical with the land in suit appertaining to Plot No. 81/123. The learned Judge on consideration of Ext. A found that Idris Miah did not furnish any particular about his pattani land in the objection case and in the written objection Ext. 7(A) in Title Suit No. 63 of 1976, the defendant No. 3 for the first time disclosed particulars of land of their settlement. It appears on the basis of an application filed by the plaintiffs, the learned Munsif appointed a survey knowing Advocate Commissioner for the purpose of investigation who submitted his report on 9.2.80 but the learned Munsif without accepting the report dismissed the suit. The learned District Judge on perusal of the report found that the Advocate Commissioner on relayment found that the land of DS Plot Nos. 22, 23, 24, 93, 94, 95, 94/1, 50, 51, 70, 71, 91, 69, 49 of No. 258 of Mouza Char Jabilee does not attract the land of Diara Block Plot No. 81/123. On consideration of this material evidence the learned District Judge held that the objection Case No. 472 of 1968 was allowed without any basis and it did not create any legal right in favour of Idris Miah. The learned District Judge further found that while on the basis of the lease the plaintiffs were in possession Abdul Kader Chowdhury filed the Miscellaneous Case. 100/75-76 for allotment of separate shaham from Block Plot No. 81/123 and got an order made in his favour and that order necessitated in institute of the Title Suit No. 63 of 1970 on 21.1.76 against Abdul Kader Chowdhury and others for permanent injunction followed an application for temporary injunction not to proceed with the demarcation of the land in pursuant to shaham allotted to the defendant No. 3 Abdul Kader Chowdhury in the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case No. 100 of 1975-76. Against the said order the plaintiffs preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 188 of 1976 and prayed for temporary injunction which was rejected by Mr. Amiya Bhushan Podder, District Judge by his order dated 30.11.76 and the appeal was subsequently dismissed by another Subordinate Judge on 24.11.74. The learned District Judge further noticed that due,to observation made in Title Suit No. 63 of 1976 several suits were filed which however were dismissed on different dates and against the decree of dismissal of Title Suit No. 465 of 1980 Title Appeal No. 11 of 1989 was preferred and during pendency of that appeal in respect of 27.50 acres of land, the defendant No. 3 petitioner herein started SA Petition Case No. 20 of 1985-86 and obtained an order 15.8.85 from the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Noakhali cancelling the lease made in favour of the plaintiff. On consideration of the aforesaid evidence the learned District Judge held that the order dated 15.8.85 of defendant No. 2 was illegal.
